written.q: Define AI and distinguish ANI, AGI and ASI with an example of each.
written.a: AI is the science of developing techniques to generate intelligence artificially. ANI (weak AI): excels at one specific task, e.g. face recognition, Siri/Alexa, Google Maps; it is the only kind that exists. AGI (strong AI): can think, learn and perform any intellectual task like a human and learn new tasks without retraining; hypothetical, e.g. a robot that can study, cook, drive and solve problems. ASI: far more intelligent than humans in every field including creativity and emotions; a future concept.

written.q: Explain the Turing Test and the Chinese Room argument.
written.a: Turing Test (1950): a human interrogator asks written questions to a hidden human and a hidden machine; if the interrogator cannot tell which is the machine, the machine is considered intelligent. Chinese Room (Searle): a person who does not understand Chinese uses a powerful rule book (knowledge base and mapping function) to give perfect Chinese answers; from outside it appears they understand, but they only follow rules. So a computer could pass the Turing Test and merely act intelligent without being intelligent.

written.q: Compare rule-based (GOFAI) and data-driven AI and explain why the data-driven approach dominates today.
written.a: GOFAI: experts write facts and rules using symbols (IF temperature > 38 THEN fever); tools Prolog, LISP, expert systems. Data-driven AI (machine learning): the machine learns patterns from data without hand-written rules. It dominates because of big data (volume, velocity, variety) and massive computing power (GPUs, TPUs, cloud computing).

written.q: Draw/describe the AI map and say where GA, fuzzy logic and swarm intelligence belong.
written.a: AI is the outer set; inside it is ML; inside ML are neural networks; inside those, deep learning (many layers); inside that, transformers such as ChatGPT. Genetic algorithms, swarm intelligence, fuzzy logic and rule-based systems are other AI techniques that sit beside ML inside AI; they can be hybridised, e.g. learning classifier systems.

written.q: Distinguish discriminative and generative AI and name three kinds of predictive task.
written.a: Discriminative (predictive) AI classifies or predicts from input data (spam detection, face recognition). Generative AI creates new content such as text, images, audio and video (ChatGPT, music generation). Predictive tasks: classification (a category), regression (a number), time-series forecasting (a future value from past values).

written.q: Describe how an intelligent system interacts with its environment and distinguish embodied from disembodied AI.
written.a: Sensors collect information from the environment; the intelligent system decides; actuators perform actions on the environment; the loop repeats. Embodied AI resides in a physical body (self-driving cars, humanoid robots); disembodied AI is software only (ChatGPT, Google Translate).
